channel.title: Nature Physics
channel.description: Nature Physics offers news and reviews alongside top-quality research papers in a monthly publication, covering the entire spectrum of physics. Physics addresses the properties and interactions of matter and energy, and plays a key role in the development of a broad range of technologies. To reflect this, Nature Physics covers all areas of pure and applied physics research. The journal focuses on core physics disciplines, but is also open to a broad range of topics whose central theme falls within the bounds of physics.

item.title: [7] Wigner crystals get dressed
item.content:encoded:
Last authors: Mauro Brotons-Gisbert, Brian D. Gerardot

Score 7/10 B_IMPORTANT_CONDMAT

Why: Important experimental study of Wigner polarons and electron correlation effects.

Tags: #Wignercrystal #correlation #spectroscopy

Abstract: When repulsion overcomes their tendency to move freely, electrons can arrange into a crystal. Two experiments have now identified Wigner polarons, quasiparticles whose optical signatures reveal the collective response of the electron lattice.

item.title: [8] Superconductivity and ferroelectric orbital magnetism in semimetallic rhombohedral hexalayer graphene
item.content:encoded:
Last authors: Kin Fai Mak, Xiaomeng Liu

Authors: Jinghao Deng, Jiabin Xie, Hongyuan Li, et al.

Score 8/10 B_IMPORTANT_CONDMAT

Why: Significant discovery of correlated states and superconductivity in a moire/graphene system.

Tags: #graphene #superconductivity #correlated

Abstract: The semimetallic regime in rhombohedral graphene has not been extensively explored. Now, correlated insulators, superconductivity and multiferroic orbital magnetic order are demonstrated in semimetallic rhombohedral hexalayer graphene.

item.title: [6] Coherent phonon control beyond amplitude saturation in a sliding ferroelectric
item.content:encoded:
Last authors: Fabio Caruso, Manfred Fiebig

Authors: Jan Gerrit Horstmann, Christoph Emeis, Andrin Caviezel, et al.

Score 6/10 B_IMPORTANT_CONDMAT

Why: Ultrafast dynamics study in WTe2 relevant to structural/electronic transition control.

Tags: #WTe2 #ultrafast #phonon

Abstract: Strong photoexcitation of phonons in a crystal can lead to a nonlinear response. Now it is shown that this breakdown of linearity can be overcome by the application of well-timed photoexcitation pulses in WTe2.
